documents.unit: Old Dominion University Board of Visitors (EVMS is now part of ODU)
documents.title: Policy 1220 Standards for the Safe Use of Artificial Intelligence
documents.summary: ODU Board of Visitors Policy 1220 sets university-wide standards for ethical, private and transparent AI use covering employees, teaching and research. It requires vendor review, data protection and annual review, and says little about student coursework.
documents.stance_why: Policy 1220 states no rules for student coursework; its standards "Encourage innovation and experimentation in AI integration" and set ethical, privacy and governance duties for employees, so the position is encourage with conditions, not delegates.

units.why: The purpose clause sets the institution-wide framework: "responsible, ethical, and transparent use of artificial intelligence". It states purpose, so P56 (framework) fits rather than P61, which is only definitions.
units.anchor: establish a culture of integrity that ensures the responsible,

units.why: The definition of AI sets what the policy covers: "the simulation of human intelligence processes by machines". A definition, so P61.
units.anchor: the simulation of human intelligence processes by machines
units.frag_end: tasks that typically require human intelligence.

units.why: Scope clause says who and what the policy binds: "all Old Dominion University employees" and "educational initiatives". It sets scope, so P61 (scope), not P56.
units.anchor: applies to all Old Dominion University employees, including staff, administrators,
units.frag_end: may be employed within the University ecosystem.

units.why: The policy statement commits to AI standards that "support research, teaching, and administration"; a principle-level framework statement, hence P56.
units.anchor: committed to the effective implementation of comprehensive artificial intelligence policy standards
units.frag_end: protecting individual data, and mitigating risk.

units.why: Standard 2 "Foster Innovation" says to "Encourage innovation and experimentation in AI integration" in teaching and learning: a default of encouragement, so P02.
units.anchor: Encourage innovation and experimentation in AI integration to enhance

units.why: Standard 1 requires ethical use, "promoting fairness, accountability, transparency and respect for human rights" in AI deployment in teaching; ethics principle, P53 (ethical concerns).
units.anchor: Prioritize ethical considerations and ethical use in AI deployment
units.frag_end: AI related activities conducted within the University.

units.why: Standard 3 commits to safeguard "privacy and security of individuals' data" with "robust data protection measures"; data protection, P50.
units.anchor: Safeguard the privacy and security of individuals' data

units.why: Standard 4 says to "Implement strategies to mitigate risks" including "biases, discrimination" of AI; names bias harms, P53.
units.anchor: including biases, discrimination, and data breaches.

units.why: Standard 5 commits to "equitable access to AI resources" for students, faculty and staff, an equity-of-access commitment, P51.
units.anchor: Ensure equitable access to AI resources and opportunities for all

units.why: Standard 6 says to "Leverage AI technologies to personalize learning experiences"; it welcomes AI use in learning, P02 (default encouragement) rather than P44 as no professional-skill claim is made.
units.anchor: Leverage AI technologies to personalize learning

units.why: Procedure 1 requires a "standardized and transparent approval process" for acquiring or deploying AI; vetting of tools, so P50 (prefer vetted tools) over P65, which concerns vendor contracts.
units.anchor: establish a standardized and transparent approval process for the acquisition,

units.why: Procedure 2a requires AI outputs in "educational settings" to carry "clear and comprehensive disclaimers" on limitations and bias; reliability and bias of AI output, P31; it is a disclaimer to users, not a student submission disclosure (P24).
units.anchor: must be accompanied by clear and comprehensive disclaimers that inform users
units.frag_start: All AI products or outcomes generated

units.why: Procedure 2b: "Promote transparency in AI usage by providing stakeholders with access to information"; institutional transparency principle, P56.
units.anchor: Promote transparency in AI usage by providing stakeholders with access

units.why: Procedure 3a requires measures to assess "risks associated with third -party AI vendors" incl. data sharing agreements; vendor review, P65.
units.anchor: assess and mitigate risks associated with third -party AI

units.why: Procedure 3b says vendor contracts "should include provisions for data protection, privacy safeguards"; contract terms, P65.
units.anchor: Contracts with AI vendors should include provisions for data protection,

units.why: Procedure 3c requires "regular audits and assessments" of third-party AI performance and security; ongoing vendor review, so P65 (the closest vendor-oversight type).
units.anchor: Conduct regular audits and assessments in collaboration with ITS

units.why: Procedure 4a requires "robust data privacy and security measures" for sensitive information in AI systems, covering students and employees; P50.
units.anchor: Implement robust data privacy and security measures to safeguard sensitive

units.why: Procedure 4b requires AI systems to comply with laws on student data "including the Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act (FERPA)"; P50 covers data protection.
units.anchor: comply with applicable laws and regulations governing the collection, storage, and use

units.why: Procedure 5a calls for stronger data privacy "when using AI technologies" in research and "informed consent"; research governance, P62.
units.anchor: Strengthen provisions related to data privacy and security when using AI technologies,

units.why: Procedure 5b requires measures so "confidential, sensitive, and other protected data are not entered into any AI research tool without proper risk analysis"; research data rule, P62 chosen over P50 because it governs research tools.
units.anchor: confidential, sensitive, and other protected data are not entered into any AI research tool
units.frag_end: other sensitive or confidential institutional research data.

units.why: Procedure 5c says AI use in research with humans or animals "should be disclosed in the Institutional Review Board (IRB) application"; research rule deferring to IRB, P62.
units.anchor: should be disclosed in the Institutional Review Board (IRB) application
units.frag_start: Any use of AI tools in

units.why: Procedure 6a commits to "training and professional development opportunities for faculty, staff, and administrators on AI ethics"; supports faculty learning, P63.
units.anchor: Provide training and professional development opportunities for faculty, staff, and administrators

units.why: Procedure 6b calls for "partnerships with industry stakeholders, government agencies" to share AI practices; no type covers partnerships for knowledge sharing and it is not a framework principle (P56), so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: Forge partnerships with industry stakeholders, government agencies, and academic institutions
units.uncovered_note: Institutional partnerships with industry, government and other institutions to exchange AI practice and build interdisciplinary AI research.

units.why: Procedure 6c sets "ongoing monitoring, evaluation, and review of AI initiatives" and soliciting stakeholder feedback; review and feedback, P54.
units.anchor: ongoing monitoring, evaluation, and review of AI initiatives

units.why: Procedure 7 requires engaging "students, faculty, staff, and the broader community in discussions and forums on AI ethics"; dialogue, not policy revision (P54), and no other type fits, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: Engage students, faculty, staff, and the broader community in discussions
units.uncovered_note: Community engagement: forums and dialogue with students, faculty, staff and local stakeholders on AI ethics, privacy and societal implications.

units.why: Procedure 8 says compliance standards are "published on the Information Technology Services Computing Policies and Standards website"; says where the policy framework is maintained, P56.
units.anchor: standards to be utilized for compliance with this policy are published
units.frag_start: The specific standards to be utilized

units.why: Section G requires "annual reviews of this policy" with consultation of experts and stakeholders; a review cycle, P54.
units.anchor: shall conduct annual reviews of this policy

documents.unit: Old Dominion University AI Implementation Workgroup
documents.title: Guidelines for Teaching and Learning with AI
documents.summary: ODU teaching guidelines encourage faculty to explore AI, leave the extent of use to each instructor and offer three sample syllabus statements. They also cover training, assignment redesign, integrity, privacy and ethics.
documents.stance_why: The guidelines give faculty "the autonomy to decide the extent to which they incorporate AI" and supply "permissive, hybrid, and restrictive" sample statements, so the stance is delegates with tiers.

units.why: The guidelines open by saying they give "clear and practical guidance" for AI in teaching and learning with an "innovative, ethical, and supportive environment"; a framework preamble, P56.
units.anchor: designed to foster an innovative, ethical, and supportive
units.frag_end: environment for AI use in education.

units.why: Principle 1 states "Faculty are encouraged to explore and integrate AI tools"; default encouragement, P02.
units.anchor: Faculty are encouraged to explore and integrate AI tools

units.why: Principle 2 says AI use "should align with ethical standards, respect data privacy, and comply with relevant regulations (FERPA, HIPAA, etc.)"; privacy, P50.
units.anchor: respect data privacy, and comply with relevant regulations (FERPA, HIPAA, etc.)
units.frag_start: AI use should align with ethical

units.why: Principle 2 also states "Transparency in AI applications is essential"; a general transparency principle, P56.
units.anchor: Transparency in AI applications is essential.

units.why: Principle 3 gives faculty "the autonomy to decide the extent to which they incorporate AI tools in their courses"; per-instructor decision, P04.
units.anchor: Faculty have the autonomy to decide the extent to which they incorporate AI

units.why: Principle 3 adds that faculty who choose not to use AI "will not be required to follow these guidelines"; leaves the decision to the instructor, P04.
units.anchor: Those who choose not to use AI will not be required

units.why: Principle 4 says training programs "will continue to be provided" so faculty and students use AI "effectively"; support for learning AI, P63.
units.anchor: Comprehensive training programs and resources will continue to be provided

units.why: DTT "will provide and continuously update AI training sessions" and faculty "are encouraged to attend"; faculty support, P63.
units.anchor: Faculty are encouraged to attend these

units.why: Principle 5 says feedback "will be used to continuously improve AI initiatives at ODU"; revisit and feedback, P54.
units.anchor: Feedback on AI tools, trainings, and resources will be used to continuously

units.why: Guideline 1 says faculty "should familiarize themselves with the capabilities and limitations of AI tools"; learning AI before course policy, P63.
units.anchor: Faculty should familiarize themselves with the capabilities and limitations of AI

units.why: Guideline 1 says "AI tools should be used to augment, not replace, human interaction and judgment"; AI must not replace human thinking, P32.
units.anchor: AI tools should be used to augment, not replace, human interaction and judgment.

units.why: Guideline 2 says faculty "should include a clear AI policy in their course syllabi"; syllabus statement, P09.
units.anchor: Faculty should include a clear AI policy in their course syllabi

units.why: Sample statements for "permissive, hybrid, and restrictive use" are provided, i.e. named levels of AI use that instructors pick from; P05.
units.anchor: Sample policy statements for permissive, hybrid, and restrictive use are provided

units.why: Guideline 3 says to "Redesign assignments to leverage AI tools where appropriate, such as generating prompts, providing feedback"; P35.
units.anchor: Redesign assignments to leverage AI tools where appropriate

units.why: Guideline 3 also says to "design assignments to promote original student work" given misuse potential; assignment redesign around AI, P35.
units.anchor: design assignments to promote original student work.

units.why: Guideline 4 says to "Clearly communicate expectations regarding the use of AI tools and the consequences of misuse"; communicating rules, P09 rather than P37 as no penalties are named.
units.anchor: Clearly communicate expectations regarding the use of AI tools

units.why: "Academic integrity misconduct will follow existing honor code and student conduct standards"; AI misuse handled under integrity processes, P36.
units.anchor: Academic integrity misconduct will follow existing honor code and student conduct standards.

units.why: Faculty "will be provided with relevant tools and trainings to detect and address potential academic misconduct related to AI"; detection tools used to identify misuse, P40.
units.anchor: tools and trainings to detect and address potential academic misconduct related to AI

units.why: Guideline 5 says to "Ensure AI use complies with copyright, intellectual property, and privacy laws"; IP and licensing, P52.
units.anchor: Ensure AI use complies with copyright, intellectual property, and privacy laws.

units.why: "Protect sensitive data and comply with FERPA and HIPAA regulations when using AI tools in teaching and learning"; P50.
units.anchor: Protect sensitive data and comply with FERPA and HIPAA regulations

units.why: Guideline 6 says to use AI "in a manner that supports diversity, inclusion, and accessibility"; equity of access, P51.
units.anchor: supports diversity, inclusion, and accessibility.
units.frag_start: Use AI tools in a manner

units.why: Faculty should "Educate students and recommend student to attend trainings" on "potential biases and limitations of AI-generated content"; teaches AI limits and bias, P53 chosen over P63 because the audience is students.
units.anchor: potential biases and limitations of AI- generated content.

units.why: DTT "will continue to update and add to the existing AI website" with use cases, alternative assignments, webinars; faculty resources, P63.
units.anchor: will continue to update and add to the existing AI website

units.why: Faculty "can coordinate with DTT to recommend or develop new training sessions"; faculty community and support, P63.
units.anchor: Faculty can coordinate with DTT to recommend or develop new training sessions

units.why: The permissive sample says the course "encourages students to explore the use of Generative AI (GenAI) tools such as ChatGPT for all assignments and assessments"; default permit/encourage, P02.
units.anchor: encourages students to explore the use of Generative AI (GenAI) tools

units.why: The permissive sample requires that "Any such use must be appropriately acknowledged and cited"; disclosure with submission, P24.
units.anchor: Any such use must be appropriately acknowledged and cited.

units.why: "It is each student's responsibility to assess the validity and applicability of any GenAI output"; students verify output, P31.
units.anchor: assess the validity and applicability of any GenAI output that is submitted

units.why: "you bear the final responsibility" for submitted GenAI output; students own what they submit, P29.
units.anchor: you bear the final responsibility.

units.why: Permissive sample: "Violations of this policy will be considered academic misconduct"; misconduct classification, P36.
units.anchor: Violations of this policy will be considered academic misconduct.

units.why: Hybrid sample says certain assignments "will permit or even encourage" GenAI, so permission is set per assignment; P04.
units.anchor: Certain assignments in this course will permit or even encourage the use

units.why: Hybrid sample sets a fallback: "The default is that such use is disallowed unless otherwise stated"; P06.
units.anchor: The default is that such use is disallowed unless otherwise stated.

units.why: Hybrid sample requires AI use be "appropriately acknowledged and cited" where allowed; disclosure, P24.
units.anchor: Any such use must be appropriately acknowledged and cited.

units.why: Hybrid sample: "you bear the final responsibility" for the validity of submitted GenAI output; verify output, P31.
units.anchor: assess the validity and applicability of any GenAI output

units.why: Hybrid sample: violations "will be considered academic misconduct"; P36.
units.anchor: Violations of this policy will be considered academic misconduct.

units.why: Restrictive sample: "all the work students submit for this course will be their own"; submitted work is the student's own, P29.
units.anchor: all the work students submit for this course will be their own.
units.frag_start: We expect that all the work

units.why: Restrictive sample: "We specifically forbid the use of ChatGPT or any other Generative AI (GenAI) tools at all stages of the work process, including preliminary ones"; a default ban on AI, P01.
units.anchor: We specifically forbid the use of ChatGPT or any other Generative AI

units.why: Restrictive sample: collaborative assignments must "list all team members who participated"; an authorship rule, P29 (work is own) fits better than P24, which is about AI disclosure.
units.anchor: we expect for the assignment to list all team members who participated.

units.why: Restrictive sample: "Violations of this policy will be considered academic misconduct"; P36.
units.anchor: Violations of this policy will be considered academic misconduct.

documents.title: Brock Virginia Health Sciences AI Guidelines
documents.summary: Thin capture of the Brock Virginia Health Sciences AI guidelines page for the medical school context. It names Policy 1220 as the authoritative framework and lists roles it serves; the core principles were not in the saved text.
documents.stance_why: The saved page has only an intro and framework note ("supports thoughtful, responsible integration") and defers to Policy 1220; it sets no rule, and the role-based principles were not captured, so delegates.

units.why: The page says VHS at ODU "supports thoughtful, responsible integration of these tools" in clinical care, medical education, and research; a framework statement of purpose, P56.
units.anchor: VHS at ODU supports thoughtful, responsible integration of these tools.
units.frag_start: As artificial intelligence changes clinical care

units.why: The framework note says guidelines "operate within the ODU institutional framework" and point to Policy 1220; it sets scope and hierarchy, P56.
units.anchor: These guidelines operate within the ODU institutional framework.
units.frag_end: medical education context at VHS at ODU.

units.why: The welcome says guidance exists for faculty "preparing medical and health professions students for AI in healthcare" and a student "learning to use these tools responsibly"; teaching AI as professional skill, P44.
units.anchor: preparing medical and health professions students for AI in healthcare
